searchText: I’d go the other way and only support finalized if anything. Then you just force cache it for a period. For checkpoint sync you don’t need it to be the very latest finalized but closer is better. Also a reason why defining a separate api makes sense so it doesn’t have the implication that the user is specifying the state to return - it should be up to the provider Yeah thats an interesting thought. I suspect theres probably a few devils in the details with all the clients currently implementing checkpoint sync slightly differently (I've roughly documented the routes here: https://notes.ethereum.org/@samcm/HJVJBRE3q). But if we're standardising how the process should happen then yeah I agree that's a simpler way to go 👍 if we set the cache header appropriately on the state route we can still make life fairly easy for caching... even if we set it to an epoch duration it'd be helpful i would expect it sounds like we could potentially just add `"finalized": true` to the `blocks/{id}/root` response... probably just at the same level as execution_optimiistic is and include if the block requested is finalized? Just to consolidate the discussion in the linked thread and <#745077610685661265> - Is the idea that clients would implement something like this? CLI args: ``` --checkpoint-sync-state-urls=https://untrusted.com --checkpoint-sync-trust-urls=http://trusted1.com,https://trusted2.com ``` On startup: - Fetch the state from a random `state-url` via `GET /eth/v2/debug/beacon/states/finalized` (which could be moved to the `/eth/v1/checkpoint` namespace) - Verify the retrieved state by checking all `trust-urls` via `GET /eth/v1/beacon/finalized_blocks/{slot}/root` - abort if a certain amount don't agree (maybe configurable?) - abort if the state is outside of the weak subjectivity period Obviously we want as many people/entities to run these endpoints as possible so I think it's worthwhile to look ahead and see how it'd look in practice. I don't think we will see as much uptake for either of these providers if it's unsafe to use a "production" beacon node as the source node - especially for home stakers. We can get away with only a handful of state providers, but the more trust providers the better. The safest way would be to handle both of these routes with a web server and return data from a directory that is updated by a cron on an interval. But potentially even that is too manual/finicky to see a large amount of uptake. As an FYI I've been experimenting with a standalone app with the current checkpoint sync implementation but if we are separating the providers by `state` and `trust` it's probably way more viable and would likely solve those problems and hopefully improve uptake. - Runs a webserver with configurable upstream nodes - Ensures the upstream nodes don't get DOS'd - Configurable to be a `state` provider or `trust` provider - Sets `cache-control` headers depending on the content - Fetches `finalized` state on a configurable interval and caches it internally - Stops serving the state if its outside the WS period - Fetches slot block roots and serves if `n%` upstreams agree - Upstream nodes could actually just be other instances of this app (!) We want these apis to be standalone though. The aim here is to define something very minimal that allows getting a state and then verifying it from a separate source. We don’t want it to be entwined in the standard rest api because that means needing to support a bunch more functionality than is required and makes it harder to provide those endpoints publicly. Ok fair… so separate base path and maybe able to just serve those specific trust endpoints…

excerpts.author: samcm
excerpts.content:
Just to consolidate the discussion in the linked thread and <#745077610685661265> - Is the idea that clients would implement something like this?

CLI args:
```
--checkpoint-sync-state-urls=https://untrusted.com
--checkpoint-sync-trust-urls=http://trusted1.com,https://trusted2.com
```

On startup:
- Fetch the state from a random `state-url` via `GET /eth/v2/debug/beacon/states/finalized` (which could be moved to the `/eth/v1/checkpoint` namespace)
- Verify the retrieved state by checking all `trust-urls` via `GET /eth/v1/beacon/finalized_blocks/{slot}/root` 
  - abort if a certain amount don't agree (maybe configurable?)
  - abort if the state is outside of the weak subjectivity period

excerpts.author: samcm
excerpts.content:
Obviously we want as many people/entities to run these endpoints as possible so I think it's worthwhile to look ahead and see how it'd look in practice. I don't think we will see as much uptake for either of these providers if it's unsafe to use a "production" beacon node as the source node - especially for home stakers. We can get away with only a handful of state providers, but the more trust providers the better.

The safest way would be to handle both of these routes with a web server and return data from a directory that is updated by a cron on an interval. But potentially even that is too manual/finicky to see a large amount of uptake.

As an FYI I've been experimenting with a standalone app with the current checkpoint sync implementation but if we are separating the providers by `state` and `trust` it's probably way more viable and would likely solve those problems and hopefully improve uptake.
- Runs a webserver with configurable upstream nodes
- Ensures the upstream nodes don't get DOS'd
- Configurable to be a `state` provider or `trust` provider
- Sets `cache-control` headers depending on the content 
- Fetches `finalized` state on a configurable interval and caches it internally
- Stops serving the state if its outside the WS period
- Fetches slot block roots and serves if `n%` upstreams agree
- Upstream nodes could actually just be other instances of this app (!)
